subject: Women's History Month Words and Music
overview: The West Medford Community Center hosted its monthly Fresh Fridays program, featuring local historian Dee Morris presenting on prominent women in Medford's history followed by a musical performance by the What the World Needs Now Interfaith Coalition Singers.

items.title: Introduction and Suffrage Poetry
items.summary: Host Terry Carter opened the Fresh Fridays program for Women's History Month and shared a poem on the American women's suffrage movement.

items.title: Interview with Historian Dee Morris
items.summary: Local historian Dee Morris discussed her educational background, her passion for historical research, and the importance of preserving the stories of civic ancestors.

items.title: Profiles of Historic Medford Women
items.summary: Morris highlighted the life stories of six notable women from Medford's past: Keziah Revalian, Sarah Bradley Fulton, Belinda Sutton, Lydia Maria Child, Amelia Earhart, and Madeline Duggar Kelly.

items.title: Community Center Announcements
items.summary: Carter shared updates regarding the center's elder lunch services, an upcoming AARP fraud protection workshop, and other local community concerts and events.

items.title: Interfaith Coalition Singers Performance
items.summary: The What the World Needs Now Interfaith Coalition Singers performed a selection of civil rights anthems, spirituals, and peace-themed songs to close out the event.
